metal.title: Apple Silicon (Metal)
metal.why_gate_is_memory: A Mac is one device with one pool, so counting GPUs says nothing about whether a model fits. Weights, KV and activations all come out of unified memory, and the ceiling that matters is what Metal will let the GPU hold, not what the box advertises.
notes: Metal caps a single MTLBuffer well below total memory -- 80.6 GiB of 128 GiB on an M5 Max. The GGUF loader avoids a file-sized buffer by materializing tensors as separate MPS allocations.
recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize is roughly 90% of physical (115.4 of 128 GiB measured on an M5 Max). The min_memory_bytes figures are physical RAM, chosen to leave that margin plus a KV pool.
No multi-device story: Apple exposes one GPU per machine, so every Metal profile is tensor_parallel_size 1 and scaling past one box means separate machines.

rtx3090.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
notes: GeForce driver disables GPU peer-to-peer, so every tensor-parallel collective stages through host memory. Profiles on this platform should prefer expert parallelism and host-offloaded tables over designs that add per-step all-reduces.

notes: Host KV tier (HostTierConnector, kv_transfer_config above): 48 GiB pinned host RAM per rank, sized for this 787 GiB A100 box. enable_cross_layers_blocks is required: it forces the packed cross-layer slab the connector needs, since the GLM-5.2 group specs are not guaranteed to resolve all-uniform (DSV4 records get the slab via the allocator's is_dsv4 gate). The 16 GiB hybrid KV pool is a ceiling, not a promise: it holds one full 262,144-token request (target fp8_ds_mla across 43 layers plus the 3-layer TurboQuant draft cache, ~9 GiB) with margin for concurrent shorter sessions, and the Metal worker shrinks it to whatever stays resident on the machine it boots on. Sizing it from artifact bytes is what broke on 2026-08-25: 80.8 GiB target + 6.5 GiB drafter looks like 87.3 GiB but loads to 93.57 GiB, and an M5 Max's Metal working set is 107.52 GiB rather than the ~115 GiB assumed here, so the pool overran the working set and served token soup at 1.1 tok/s. On that machine the worker now grants ~9.6 GiB. Higher API concurrency drains in scheduler waves instead of paging model weights.
max_model_len is 262144 for real (agentic) use. The 1k-in/2k-out benchmark matrix in perf/baseline_status.md is re-gated under this sizing (see the M1 Ultra campaign entries).

max_num_batched_tokens is 2176 = 2048 + 32 seqs x 4 speculative slots: the scheduler reserves draft-token room, so 2048 would cap scheduled prefill tokens at 1920 and split a 2048-token prompt into two chunks (measured ~230 ms scheduler boundary plus an inefficient 128-token tail chunk).

Long-context status (2026-08-23): the sparse-MLA indexer chain (fused indexer Q rope/quant, prefill top-k, scoring) has a native Metal implementation. Async output copies and their completion event stay on the producing MPS stream (unit-tested), which is believed to remove the cold cross-stream event ordering failure; the deterministic cold-boot wedge repro (primer then a direct multi-chunk prefill) has not been re-run, so the boot-ramp protocol in perf/prefill_handoff.md remains the ops guidance until it is. Prefill top-k sizes native work from the active request window and streams windows above 1,024 candidates with fixed scratch; the 65,536-candidate native oracle matches the eager chain on tie ordering and the streaming loop (its all-zero-query block does not exercise scoring). Full 262,144-token end-to-end serving still needs a dedicated long-context validation pass.

linear_backend must be auto, not this fork's aiter default: the aiter filter leaves no NVFP4 kernel at all, and the aiter FP8 scaled-mm kernels refuse this model's untuned GEMM shapes (e.g. the 16384x5120 GDN qkvz projection). kv_cache_dtype must be 'auto': this fork defaults the cache to fp8 for its GLM target, and the hybrid GDN/full-attention cache has only been validated at auto here.

DFlash 2 speculation is on by default: the drafter evaluates the first 3 draft positions of its trained 8-token block against target layers [5, 19, 33, 47, 61], keeps top-16 candidates per position, and walks one path via the rank-256 selector. enable_prefix_caching true is SlimServe policy: every profile states it explicitly; hybrid models otherwise inherit vLLM's silent hybrid default of OFF and pay full history re-prefill every chat turn. max_cudagraph_capture_size 256 = (1 + k) x max_num_seqs for DFlash k=3 at 64 sequences, the same rule the qwen38-nvfp4-1 MI300X record follows at 192 for MTP k=2. The c1 and c8 numbers in the notebook are unaffected -- c8 is 8 x 4 = 32 rows, inside either ceiling -- so this widens graph coverage for c9..c64 rather than restating a measurement.

A fixed 96 GiB KV pool rather than gpu_memory_utilization: the utilization path runs an 8192-token profiling forward to measure free memory, which costs 142 s of Triton JIT on this model's GDN kernels and more than doubles boot. 96 GiB is half the card, comfortably above what 262144 tokens x 16 paged layers needs, and leaves the rest for the vision tower, the drafter and graph pools.

qwen38fn-fp8-8.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 on 8 GPUs
qwen38fn-fp8-8.summary: Vision-language 125B-A6B hybrid (Gated DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention, 1-in-4 full attention, 4-branch gated residual) with 51B n-gram embeddings held in pinned host memory. FP8 experts run expert-parallel through Marlin W8A16 on 8x RTX 3090.

notes: enable_expert_parallel is a correctness requirement, not a tuning choice: moe_intermediate_size is 640 and the FP8 block scales are [128, 128], so a TP shard of 80 cannot carry exact block scales. EP keeps 64 whole experts per rank (640 = 5 x 128).

moe_backend and linear_backend must be auto, not this fork's aiter defaults: AITER kernels do not exist on CUDA, and the forced-backend path raises at load ('FP8 MoE backend AITER does not support ... device cuda'). Both the top-level flags and kernel_config must be set, since a non-auto top-level flag overwrites kernel_config (same rule the qwen38-nvfp4-1 MI300X profile documents for linear_backend).
SM86 has no FP8 tensor cores and Triton FP8 MoE requires SM89+, so the experts run the Marlin W8A16 block-FP8 MoE kernels (weight-only decode to BF16 compute).

VLLM_QWEN4_EXP_PLE_HOST=1 keeps the full 47.7 GiB n-gram (PLE) table pinned in host RAM per rank and gathers the 16 rows per token (2560 bytes) from the GPU over UVA inside the forward, exactly as the model card intends ('tables prefetched from host memory'). The gather is graph-capturable, so FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture keeps working, and the TP-replicated table removes the per-step embedding all-reduce that this no-P2P platform cannot afford. Host cost: ~48 GiB pinned per rank (~382 GiB total of the 996 GiB box).

Multi-GPU GeForce runs fine on the stock NVIDIA driver but leaves 36-58% of TP throughput on the table: install QuixiAI's P2P driver (github.com/QuixiAI/open-gpu-kernel-modules, see docs/geforce-p2p.md) for direct GPU-GPU DMA. Measured on this profile: c1 109.6->148.8 (+36%), c8 409.7->647.9 (+58%). NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS in this env is required for P2P across root complexes and harmless on stock drivers.
reasoning_parser qwen3 and tool_call_parser qwen3_xml: the template thinks in <think> blocks and calls tools with <function=...> XML.
Speculation uses the checkpoint's own single-layer QSA MTP drafter (Qwen4ExpMTP) via method 'mtp'; there is no separate DSpark artifact for this model yet.

Main QSA KV is fp8 (float8_e4m3fn, unit scale) at the native max_model_len 262144 via kv_cache_dtype fp8 (operator decision 2026-09-02, reversing the 2026-08-28 bf16 mandate; NOT TurboQuant). The layer stores only the main QSA KV in fp8 - the indexer's compressed cache, the raw-key ring and the GDN state keep their own dtypes - and the sparse-gather kernel decodes e4m3 arithmetically in-register (SM86 has no fp8 cvt). The fp8 path was removed 2026-08-27 (de0b2af8a) and restored 2026-09-02; VLLM_QWEN4_EXP_FP8_MAIN_KV=1 is the equivalent layer-scoped diagnostic switch. Capacity: bf16 held 269,155 tokens = 1.03x one max-length request in the 3.64 GiB/rank pool; fp8 halves the dominant slab. Measured cost (2026-08-27 A/B, pre tile-fix): ~10% c1 / ~25% c8 vs bf16; the quantized-KV tile fix (block_n 16 / 4 warps) has since removed the wide-tile collapse that dominated that c8 loss. Requalified on-box 2026-09-02 (perf/optimization_status.md): GPU KV cache 496,174 tokens = 1.89x one max-length request in the same 3.64 GiB/rank (attention block 800 tokens), tier eviction-restore recall and 3-seed multi-turn tracking PASS, exact 1000/2000 c1 135.7 / c8 590-594 / c32 1,017-1,101 tok/s: c1/c8 at bf16 parity, c32 ~7-8% under bf16 (arithmetic e4m3 decode at the 96-row verify width; LUT decode is the open lead).

max_num_seqs 32 with max_cudagraph_capture_size 96: at MTP k=2 every decode step is seqs x 3 query tokens, so 96 covers full-batch decode steps with FULL graphs (c32 measured 425 tok/s eager vs 880 graphed). Raising max_num_seqs requires raising the capture size with it (3 x max_num_seqs) or the largest batches silently run eager.
The QSA sparse-gather kernel pins narrow tiles (block_n 16, 4 warps) for quantized KV: the wide-tile profile that suits bf16 collapses in-register dequant 3.8x (TQ) to 23x (fp8) at 48+ token steps.

min_host_ram_bytes gates this platform at 128 GiB system RAM: the 47.7 GiB n-gram (PLE) table is pinned ONCE in a /dev/shm segment shared by all TP ranks (not per rank), plus load staging and runtime headroom. A machine that passes the GPU gate but lacks the RAM fails at plan time instead of dying mid-load.

Dynamic speculative decoding is supported and measured: adding 'num_speculative_tokens': 3 and 'num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size': [[1,4,3],[5,32,2]] to speculative_overrides (with max_cudagraph_capture_size 128) buys +19.5% at concurrency 4 for -2.6% at concurrency 32 (824 vs 846 tok/s, fully explained by k=3 ramp/drain acceptance). Static k=2 stays the default because c32 is this profile's peak; flip the overrides for latency-shaped traffic. The V2 runner captures one uniform-decode graph family per scheduled k, clipped to each k's batch range.

gpu_memory_utilization 0.96, not 0.9: this hybrid's packed KV slab charges every running request ~13-14 blocks at chat context (QSA token blocks at 1056 tokens/block, one compressor ring block, 3 GDN state blocks at MTP k=2, plus the drafter's cache group), and at 0.9 the ~2.2 GiB/rank pool holds ~373 blocks = 27 requests -- the scheduler silently caps below max_num_seqs 32 with the KV meter at 100%. 0.95 sizes the pool for the full 32 with margin. Found by WildChat multi-turn replay (2026-08-27). Raised again 0.95 -> 0.96 on 2026-08-28: bf16 KV at the native 262144 needs 3.55 GiB/rank and 0.95 provides 3.41 (startup check fails 140 MB short); 0.96 provides ~3.65 with ~0.4 GiB true free after the profiled activation and graph reserves.

VLLM_ADMISSION_MAX_CONCURRENT=96 caps total in-flight generation requests (decode slots plus engine queue) at 3x max_num_seqs; beyond that the API server answers 429 + Retry-After instead of letting the queue grow without bound. Measured at 64 concurrent sessions, oversubscription past 32 buys zero throughput (780.5 vs 779.7 tok/s) and only queueing delay (TTFT p50 40.2s vs 11.6s), so the cap exists to shed pathological load, not to police normal bursts: naive clients that burst to 60-90 requests still queue and complete. Non-generation routes (models, health, metrics) are never capped.

Prefix caching is ON (TurboQuant main-KV + mamba cache mode 'align', correctness validated 2026-08-27: byte-identical cached/uncached greedy outputs, 504/504 WildChat replay, -1.5% KV capacity). The mamba-page alignment forces 1056-token cache blocks, so hits require shared prefixes of at least one full block: shallow chats (~2K histories) measured only a 2.2% hit rate for ~4% peak throughput, but deep multi-turn traffic is transformed - a 100K-token history is ~94 cached blocks and each turn re-prefills only the tail, versus re-paying the entire history every turn with caching off (measured: the engine degenerates to ~5K tok/s prefill / ~20 tok/s generation on deep conversations). Finer-grained caching needs decoupling the attention block from the mamba state snapshot (open kernel/allocator work).

enable_prefix_caching true is SlimServe policy (2026-08-28): every profile states it explicitly; hybrid models otherwise inherit vLLM's silent hybrid default of OFF and pay full history re-prefill every chat turn. Validated on rtx3090: byte-identical cached/uncached greedy outputs, 504/504 WildChat replay, -1.5% KV capacity.

Host KV tier (HostTierConnector, kv_transfer_config above) is ENABLED and validated on this box (2026-08-28; resized 2026-09-02): 88 GiB pinned host RAM per rank (704 GiB total) = 15,773 block slots x 800 tokens = ~12.6M tokens of evicted-conversation capacity behind the ~496K-token GPU pool, leaving ~188 GB MemAvailable on this 995 GB box with the 48 GiB shared PLE table (a 104 GiB/rank tier would leave ~60 GB - too little for prefill staging and page cache). The arena is cudaHostRegister-ed at exactly its size: torch's pin_memory=True allocator rounds to the next power of two, which turned 88 and 104 GiB into 128 GiB/rank and OOM-killed the boot (2026-09-02); 64 GiB only ever fit because it is a power of two. Tail states ride the engine's own frozen align-mode boundary snapshots (pool prefix cache, looked up by boundary hash - never live blocks); restores land at position k-1 per mamba group and the QSA ring is zeroed defensively. Validated: multi-depth marker-recall acceptance (8K/24K/42K restored sub-second after full GPU-pool eviction, outputs byte-identical to GPU-cache controls at 8K/24K), throughput-neutral (c1 133.6 / c8 599.4 / c32 1,149.7 vs 1,151.2 no-tier baseline). Known limitation: one tail per trajectory - a sibling re-ask after a deeper follow-up turn re-prefills instead of resuming (correct, just slower); resume boundaries exist at ~2K-token chunk ends, so sub-chunk (<2K) conversations are not tier-resumable (re-prefill is faster anyway). Raw: perf/results/2026-08-28/kv-tier/. Third tier (2026-09-02, resized 2026-09-03 for the dedicated 3.7 TB nvme1n1 XFS mount): nvme_tier_gb_per_rank 448 writes every confirmed host block through to a per-rank O_TMPFILE on the tier device (directory from SLIMSERVE_KV_TIER_DIR, else $SLIMSERVE_CACHE/kv-tier, else ~/.cache/slimserve/kv-tier - never a path in this file); 448 GiB/rank (3.5 TiB total on the dedicated device) = 80,273 slots x 800 tokens = ~64M tokens of evicted conversations that survive host-tier eviction (demotion keeps the disk copy; a hit promotes disk -> host -> GPU). Validated on port 8001 with a 2 GiB host tier forcing demotion: marker recall PASS at 8K/24K/42K restored from NVMe in 1.3/1.5/2.5 s (cold 2.1/6.0/10.0 s). The dedicated device is nvme1n1 (XFS, /mnt/kvtier, operator fstab + SLIMSERVE_KV_TIER_DIR); see perf/optimization_status.md 2026-09-03 for the greedy recall validation of the promoted path.

Chat-template defaults: reasoning_effort low (the template ships xhigh, which spends hundreds of thinking tokens on trivial turns) and preserve_thinking explicitly true (the template treats undefined as true; pinned so a template update cannot silently flip it). Per-request values override both.

glm53-nvfp4-4.title: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on 4 GPUs
glm53-nvfp4-4.summary: Vision-language 169B hybrid (34 KDA linear-attention layers + 11 DeepSeek-sparse-attention layers with a pooled indexer, mHC hyper-connections, 288-expert MoE). NVFP4 experts on Marlin, sparse NoPE MLA through the QuixiCore Ampere kernels, TP4 with experts sharded (EP measured slower).

notes: Context comes from config.json (max_position_embeddings 1048576); KV is ~17 KiB/token per rank (11 NoPE-MLA layers at 512 bf16 + 11 pooled-indexer rows at 256 bf16, KDA state is fixed-size), so the model default fits the pool at utilization 0.85.

enable_expert_parallel is off by measurement: with 288 experts at moe_intermediate 2048 the TP shard (512/rank) stays aligned to the NVFP4 group-16 scales, and the expert-parallel arm measured 4-6% slower at c1 and c8 on the optimized path (exact-token, perf/results/2026-09-01/glm53-ep-ab-opt/).

attention_config backend is explicit: the Ampere MLA priority list carries no dense MLA by design, and the DSA layers must run sparse (index_topk 2048 over 4-token pools) through QUIXICORE_MLA_SPARSE's NoPE (512-wide) kernel; sparse_mla_force_mqa keeps prefill on the same top-k MQA path.
block_size 64 is required by the pooled-indexer cache backend (DSV3.2 indexer metadata, kernel block 64).
kv_cache_dtype auto is required: this fork defaults the cache to fp8, and no Ampere MLA backend serves fp8 at the 512-wide NoPE head; bf16 main KV is also the a100 serving policy.

moe_backend marlin (top-level and kernel_config, since a non-auto top-level flag overwrites kernel_config): this fork defaults to aiter, which is ROCm-only; Marlin W4A16 is the NVFP4 MoE path on sm80.
reasoning_parser and tool_call_parser glm47: GLM-5.3 uses the GLM-4.7-family thinking and tool-call markup; enable_auto_tool_choice and thinking are the registry serving defaults.

No host KV tier on this record yet: the packed cross-layer slab the HostTierConnector requires assumes one block size across groups, and this layout mixes KDA state groups (per-request state pages) with 64-token MLA and indexer pages, so the generic packed planner mis-sizes the attention views (the rtx3090 GDN+attention profile uses the dedicated CSA-linear planner instead). Enabling the tier here is the standing follow-up: generalize that planner to KDA+MLA layouts, then run the eviction-restore acceptance.
